subsystems.name: Interior heat engine
subsystems.role: keeps water liquid with no star, using heat from radioactive decay, leftover formation heat and tidal flexing.

subsystems.name: Volatile inventory
subsystems.role: the water and gases the planet carries with it from its birth system, or captures later.

subsystems.name: Atmosphere and surface
subsystems.role: a thick hydrogen envelope slows heat loss and can hold a surface ocean above freezing.

subsystems.name: Observational network
subsystems.role: finds free-floating planets by microlensing and measures their mass and abundance.

subsystems.name: Thermal and geophysical models
subsystems.role: calculate whether an ocean survives for billions of years.

subsystems.name: Magnetic and radiation environment
subsystems.role: an internal dynamo would deflect galactic cosmic rays that otherwise erode a biosphere.

buildSteps.title: Detect the event
buildSteps.detail: A microlensing survey watches millions of stars; when a foreground mass passes in front of one, its gravity briefly brightens the background star. A short, single peak with no visible host suggests a planetary-mass lens.

buildSteps.title: Confirm it is unbound
buildSteps.detail: Follow-up imaging and parallax measurements check that the lens is not simply a planet on a very wide orbit around a faint star.

buildSteps.title: Weigh it
buildSteps.detail: Mass comes from the duration of the brightening combined with the distance to the lens; distances are the hardest part and dominate the uncertainty.

buildSteps.title: Build the abundance statistics
buildSteps.detail: Only many events, from several survey sites at different longitudes, give the mass distribution and the total number of free-floating planets.

buildSteps.title: Estimate the internal heat budget
buildSteps.detail: Models add radiogenic heating, tidal heating from any moon or from a past close encounter, and residual formation heat, then subtract conduction and radiation losses.

buildSteps.title: Model ocean persistence
buildSteps.detail: Coupled interior and atmosphere codes test whether liquid water survives for billions of years, and how thick the ice lid becomes.

buildSteps.title: Test against local analogues
buildSteps.detail: Europa and Enceladus show tidal heating sustaining subsurface oceans; Titan adds a thick atmosphere; Pluto shows how small a body can be and still be geologically active.

buildSteps.title: Look for atmospheres and aurorae
buildSteps.detail: Infrared spectroscopy of young, still-warm rogue planets can reveal atmospheric composition; radio searches look for auroral emission from a magnetic field.

buildSteps.title: Search for biosignatures
buildSteps.detail: In principle, disequilibrium gases in an atmosphere would be evidence of life — but no instrument today can make that measurement on a cold, dark, distant world.

prerequisites.why: microlensing is the only method sensitive to planets of almost any mass that are not bound to a star.
verified in our own solar system at Io, Europa and Enceladus, and the main proposed heat source for a starless ocean.
radiogenic and convective cooling over billions of years is modelled, but poorly constrained for unseen planets.

prerequisites.tech: Infrared spectroscopy of cold, faint planets
prerequisites.why: needed to detect an atmosphere, but only young, warm rogue planets are currently bright enough.

prerequisites.tech: In-situ access to an interstellar planet
prerequisites.why: no mission can reach even the nearest free-floating planet; everything must be inferred remotely.

pathway.milestone: ground-based microlensing networks have found dozens of free-floating planet candidates
pathway.unlocks: a first rough handle on how common starless planets are, with large uncertainties.

pathway.milestone: a dedicated space microlensing survey, planned as NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope
pathway.unlocks: a statistical census down to Earth-mass free-floaters and a reliable mass function — the number that decides whether such worlds matter.

pathway.milestone: infrared spectra of young, warm rogue planets
pathway.unlocks: first real constraints on their atmospheres, clouds and heat retention.

pathway.milestone: subsurface-ocean results from Europa Clipper, JUICE and Dragonfly
pathway.unlocks: calibrated rules for how much internal heating is needed to keep an ocean liquid for billions of years.

pathway.milestone: any direct study of a nearby rogue planet
pathway.unlocks: the only way to test habitability directly rather than by modelling; no mission concept exists.
